title: FirstQFM Foundation Model Cuts Quantum Gate Times by 33% on QuantWare QPU via NVIDIA Computing - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
Quantum machine learning developer FirstQFM AB has announced hardware-validated benchmarking results demonstrating a 33% reduction in single-qubit gate execution times on QuantWare’s 21-qubit Contralto-D21 superconducting quantum processor (QPU), executed without degradation in gate fidelity.

Ahead of NVIDIA GTC Berlin 2026, the company demonstrated how its patented quantum foundation model technology integrates with Quantum Machines‘ OPX control hardware and QUA calibration stack to generate zero-shot, pulse-level single-qubit gate optimizations directly from existing calibration data without requiring additional QPU runtime. The hardware tests were validated at the Israeli Quantum Computing Center (IQCC) using randomized benchmarking.

Developing the foundation model leveraged NVIDIA accelerated computing infrastructure—including the Leonardo supercomputer and the open-source NVIDIA CUDA-Q platform—before fine-tuning for QuantWare’s hardware. In addition to single-qubit speedups, the model identified pulse modifications that enhanced two-qubit Bell-state fidelities across five selected qubit pairs, addressing cross-talk and drift as QuantWare scales toward its larger VIO-based superconducting QPU architectures.

The achievement complements QuantWare’s VIO QPU architecture scaling roadmap, builds upon QuantWare’s 3D chiplet interconnect strategy, and expands NVIDIA’s CUDA-Q platform deployment across European quantum hubs.
